Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/licensing (ETL tools, temporary DB instances)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on backlog point sizing and role rate card only.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended effort, adjusted per task complexity and role mix (e.g., data migration and payment integration weighted higher for risk).

Backend Developer at 1.5 FTE (≈ 2400 hrs over a ~16-week project window) is the primary bottleneck given heavy backend-weighted backlog (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit, multi-currency); allocated hours are close to full capacity.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (≈ 960 hrs available) is thinly staffed relative to a 24-task backlog spanning security, payments and migration; allocated 750 hrs assumes reduced regression depth on Low priority items.
DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE (≈ 640 hrs available) is allocated only 350 hrs, focused on CI/staging setup, observability and decommissioning; ongoing operational support beyond this is out of scope.
Frontend Developer at 1.0 FTE (≈ 1600 hrs available) allocated 1500 hrs covers component library, dashboards, invoice views, accessibility and responsive layout work.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) and payment integration (PW-7) are treated as highest technical risk items and carry extra QA/DevOps time beyond raw point sizing.
Estimate assumes a single delivery team working sequentially through priority tiers (Urgent > High > Medium > Low) rather than fully parallel workstreams.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for tooling/licensing/audit; actual vendor quotes not yet obtained.
Project timeline assumed to be roughly 4-5 months based on team capacity and backlog size.
input.reasoning: Backlog totals 24 tasks / ~206 story points across Urgent, High, Medium and Low priorities. Given the rate card, Backend Developer is the dominant role because most high-value work (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit, multi-currency, rate limiting) is backend-heavy, and at only 1.5 FTE this role is the capacity constraint — hours were allocated near its practical ceiling (~2100 of ~2400 available hours over the estimated delivery window) with an explicit assumption flag. Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) absorbs the design system, dashboards, invoice UI, accessibility and responsive work at ~1500 hrs. QA Engineer (0.6 FTE, ~960 hrs available) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE, ~640 hrs available) are both thinly staffed relative to backlog scope, so hours were kept proportionate to their capacity rather than padded, with a caveat that this limits regression coverage and infra hardening depth. Costs were built bottom-up per role using the exact rate card figures. Non-labour costs cover realistic ancillary spend (migration tooling, accessibility audit, email provider setup, Stripe sandbox, infra contingency). Three scenarios (P20/P50/P80) reflect uncertainty mainly driven by the data migration task (PW-8, 21 points, high technical risk) and payment integration (PW-7), which are the two biggest sources of potential overrun. Priority breakdown allocates cost roughly proportional to story points within each tier, weighted slightly higher for Urgent/High items given their complexity (auth, payments, RBAC).
